rows.grounds: compound of śārdūla (tiger) and atta (attacked/eaten) with possessive ending; refers to one seized by a tiger
names the divine powers associated with the stated condition

items.question: What accomplishment and deities are associated with one attacked by a tiger?
premises: A forest accomplishment is named in this context.
The condition concerns one attacked by a tiger.
Specific deities are identified for that condition.
items.inference: The verse assigns a forest accomplishment and corresponding deities to the case of a person attacked by a tiger.
uncertainties: The exact referent of devatāḥ may depend on the preceding verses.
The precise ritual sense of vanyasiddhiḥ in this context is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: There is forest accomplishment, and for one attacked by a tiger, these are the deities.
